thread:
eli: Heads-up — AcmeAnalytics on private (VPC) is seeing 401s. They claim their client includes Authorization but our backend sees none. Customer cluster is dedicated and behind Istio ingress.

maya: can you paste the exact repro curl and the HTTP response they see?

eli: customer sent this sanitized curl:

```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
```

Response they get:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{\"error\":\"missing authorization\"}
```

eli: ingressgateway logs (tail):

```
[2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] ingressgateway-5f8f6: \"GET /v1/generate\" 401 - \"10.0.4.12\" \"curl/7.86.0\" - - - -
```

kevin: any RequestAuthentication or EnvoyFilters in that namespace? JWT policies can interact with Authorization tokens.

eli: there is a RequestAuthentication on namespace=acme-prod for their SSO provider:

```
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: RequestAuthentication
metadata:
  name: acme-jwt
  namespace: acme-prod
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-backend
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: \"https://sso.acme.com/\"
    jwksUri: \"https://sso.acme.com/.well-known/jwks.json\"
```

jackie: RequestAuthentication normally validates JWTs but doesn't strip Authorization. However, custom EnvoyFilter plugins at GATEWAY can mutate headers/payloads.

eli: customer shared a mesh-scoped EnvoyFilter that looks suspicious:

```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: strip-sensitive-headers
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
      listener:
        portNumber: 443
        filterChain:
          transportProtocol: TLS
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_AFTER
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_lowercase
        typed_config: {}
```

andre: that filter name isn't one of the standard Envoy core filters. If it's a third-party plugin that rewrites or normalizes headers it could be dropping Authorization (case-sensitive) or moving it to a different header bucket.

kevin: quick check — eli, can you exec into the ingress pod and curl the backend svc directly, preserving Authorization header, to see if it reaches the app?

eli: did that test from ingress pod:

```
kubectl -n istio-system exec -it ingressgateway-5f8f6 -- sh -c \"curl -sS -D - -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' http://redwood-backend.acme-prod.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/generate\"
```

Result: backend returns 401 and logs show no Authorization header received.

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{\"error\":\"missing authorization\"}
```

maya: reproduced. Immediate mitigation: add an early Lua filter on the gateway that copies Authorization into a safe forwarded header before other filters run. Example patch we pushed to staging:

```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: preserve-auth-header-workaround
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.lua
        typed_config:
          \"@type\": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local auth = request_handle:headers():get(\"authorization\")
              if auth ~= nil then
                request_handle:headers():add(\"x-forwarded-authorization\",\"\" .. auth)
              end
            end
```

eli: applied the Lua EnvoyFilter to staging and prod (with customer OK). After applying, we saw backend receive x-forwarded-authorization and requests succeeded.

```
[2026-03-12T14:20:01Z] redwood-backend: got header x-forwarded-authorization: Bearer test
[2026-03-12T14:20:01Z] redwood-backend: request OK -> 200
```

jackie: good short-term fix. Long-term options:
- ask customer to remove/replace the unknown header_to_lowercase plugin
- recommend Istio upgrade/patch if it's a known ABI/filter bug
- add preserve-filter to private deployment bootstrap, gated by operator flag
- consider backend fallback to x-forwarded-authorization (requires security review)

andre: security note: copying Authorization into another header is sensitive. If we keep this pattern, ensure the header is only writable by ingress, strip it before any logs, and add guidance in our security checklist.

kevin: additional context: older Istio 1.17 builds can misbehave with out-of-tree filters compiled against different Envoy ABIs and accidentally clear header maps. Acme is on 1.17.2; recommendation: upgrade to 1.17.4 (contains ABI compatibility fixes) but customer may be unable to upgrade immediately.

eli: action items agreed:
- eli: leave Lua preserve-auth EnvoyFilter in place for Acme until we have a safer default (DONE: staging+prod)
- maya: draft a Private deployment runbook section about third-party gateway filters and how to preserve Authorization headers (ETA: today COB)
- kevin: validate upstream Istio patch and propose minimal backport for our curated private images (ETA: 48h)
- andre: produce a security checklist for header forwarding and logging controls (ETA: 72h)
- jackie: add alerting: if client presents Authorization but backend responds 401 and ingress logs show header present, trigger pager (ETA: 24h)

maya: I'll also add an e2e test that applies a dummy header-mutating EnvoyFilter and verifies our preserve-filter survives and Authorization reaches the app.

eli: customer accepted temporary workaround; I'm sending status update now.

deploy-bot: Deployment applied: EnvoyFilter preserve-auth-header-workaround -> istio-system (rollout complete)

kevin: once we have a safe backport, consider adding preserve-filter to operator-managed bootstrap, opt-in via a flag, coordinate with compliance for log redaction.

andre: also run a fleet-wide grep for EnvoyFilter resources with names like strip*, header*, lowercase* that could indicate problematic filters.

eli: created an internal issue and assigned to kevin/andre/maya. Support ticket #2347 updated.

jackie: summary for records: root cause — nonstandard/third-party EnvoyFilter at gateway mutated header map and caused Authorization to be dropped; resolution — temporary Lua EnvoyFilter to copy auth into x-forwarded-authorization; follow-ups — patch/backport, runbook, e2e test, security checklist, fleet scan.

eli: wrapping up — will close the support loop and link to this thread in the ticket.
